# kar-foldcycle

> The fold-cycle: recycling held compute-state instead of recomputing it, measured on real local models.
> Deterministic verdict kernels (no LLM judge), built by Kar of the FallForge estate. MIT-licensed.

## Mechanism 1 — prefix recycling (the proven seed)
- Reuse a prompt's cached KV-state instead of recomputing the prefill.
- Result: cold ~4392 ms → warm ~240 ms = ~95% prefill-latency cut on llama3.2:1b. Control (unrelated
  queries) got no saving. Metric = real Ollama prompt_eval_duration (proxy for prefill energy, not a wattmeter).
- Honest: prefix caching is the proven seed (Ollama does it by default); this quantifies the magnitude.

## Mechanism 2 — capacity-pooling (the novel step)
- When a memory fold expires (the strand decides 'expire'), release its computed embedding to a content-keyed
  pool; reuse it when the content recurs instead of recomputing an expensive embedding-model call.
- Result: ~67% of real nomic-embed-text calls avoided (45 → 15) and ~67% embed time saved on a recurring
  workload. Control (all-unique content) got no saving — the effect requires recurrence.
- Honest: the novelty is releasing an EXPIRED fold's capacity back into the cycle; the win holds because the
  recycled computation is a real, expensive embedding.

## Not yet built
- Mechanism 3 — the balance condition that keeps the pool full across a live query-stream.

## Key files
- foldcycle.mjs / capacitypool.mjs — the two deterministic verdict kernels (WIN/LEARN/UNMEASURED/SUSPECT),
  both mutation-gated by witness.
- run-eval.mjs / run-mech2.mjs — the measurement harnesses (hit local Ollama; write results.json / results-mech2.json).
